overview: White plays the Torre set-up with Bg5, e3, Nbd2 and c3 against Black's King's Indian-style fianchetto. Black plays ...Bg7, ...O-O and ...d6 or ...d5, often hitting the centre with ...c5 or ...Ne4. White aims for a solid, easy-to-play structure with e4 or c4 later, and the game stays quiet and manoeuvring.

white_ideas.idea: Develop Bg5, e3, Nbd2, Bd3 or c3 and later e4.
Play without long theory, answering Black's set-up with the same system.

black_ideas.idea: Fianchetto the king's bishop and castle, then challenge with ...c5 or ...d5.
Hit the Bg5 with ...Ne4 or ...h6 and gain the bishop pair or tempi.

typical_structures.structure: White pawns on d4, e3 and c3 with a bishop on g5; Black fianchetto with ...d6 and ...c5 or ...d5.

character.notes: Quiet, manoeuvring play; neither side takes early risks.

structure.notes: Centre not yet fixed: d4 against ...d6 or ...d5, tension on c5/e5.

approach.notes: The Torre is a system played against most Black set-ups.

level.notes: Clear plans, little to memorise; the Bg5 is exposed to ...Ne4 though.

character.reason: Quiet but not especially hard to break down for White.

structure.reason: Centre stays undecided in the Torre.

approach.reason: The Torre set-up is played against almost anything.

level.reason: Clear plans but real positional subtleties.

plans.reason: Black's g7 bishop on the long diagonal.
